title: Relume Alternatives That Are Actually Better
summary: Relume alternatives sorted by the step they replace: sitemaps with Octopus.do, Flowmapp or Slickplan, design in Figma, build and host in Framer or Webflow.
body_markdown:
Key takeaways:


- Five of the nine tools after ours generate a sitemap from a prompt: Claritee and Octopus.do on every plan including free, Flowmapp and Slickplan from Pro, and Mockflow, whose AI page says AI credits come on every plan.
- On Relume Publish, a custom-domain site with Pro AI costs $26 a month billed yearly, or $40 monthly, by our math, and exports need a separate per-user seat.
- Webflow and React export start on Relume's Starter seat, $18 a user a month on yearly billing, and Starter stops at one project and five pages.
- Relume has no direct Framer export, so Framer users go through Relume's Figma file and Framer's Figma plugin, then fix each layout by hand.


Several of the Relume alternatives lists ranking today describe a tool that has moved on: a Webflow component library with an AI sitemap on top. Relume now does two jobs. Its Site Builder turns a brief into a sitemap, wireframes and a style guide and exports them to Figma, Webflow or React, and Relume Publish, in beta since August 24, 2026, hosts the finished site.


So decide which step to replace. We grouped the nine tools after ours by the first Relume step each takes over, in Relume's own order: sitemap, wireframe and design, build and host, then component library. Inside a group, the cheapest annually billed paid plan for that step goes first; for sitemaps, that means the cheapest paid plan with AI sitemaps, or, where the vendor doesn't say which plan has them, its cheapest paid plan.


[Awesomic](https://www.awesomic.com/) sits at number one because it's our product, and it fits none of these groups, so check what it lacks before what it does. We read each price on this page on November 13, 2026.


## Why people look past Relume


The friction with Relume shows up in four places: the bill, the page limit, the shared library and the Framer handoff.


### One site, up to three charges


Relume's pricing page carries two price systems. On the Publish side, hosting is per site: Free puts you on a relumesite.ai subdomain with a Relume badge and 1,500 monthly page views, while Launch hosting is $12 per site a month billed yearly, or $16 monthly. AI usage is per account, with Pro at $14 a month billed yearly, or $24 monthly.


Exports are the other system, and a third charge billed per user. Starter is $18 a user a month billed yearly, or $26 monthly, Pro is $40 or $58, and Team is $36 or $52 with a three-person minimum. Free exports to Figma only, so any Webflow or React handoff starts on a paid seat.


### The five-page ceiling


Starter caps you at one project and five pages. In an r/webflow thread asking[Is Relume still good?](https://www.reddit.com/r/webflow/comments/1p18vcj/is_relume_still_good/) , one user wrote that it's "a hefty price for $40 since almost every site has more than 5 pages". The thread's top reply raised a different problem: yes for wireframing, but "for webflow dev. hard no. client first is outdated". Both are anecdotes, but the cap itself is on Relume's pricing page.


### Layouts that look alike


Relume's homepage describes its AI as "Assembled, not generated": it picks from components Relume's designers built rather than writing raw code. That keeps layouts tidy, and it also means every Relume customer draws on the same library. If a client's competitors used Relume too, the sites can start to resemble each other.


### No route to Framer


Relume exports to Figma, Webflow, and React or plain HTML, and not to Framer, so a Framer team imports Relume's Figma output with Framer's plugin and checks each layout. If you're still choosing between the two builders, our[Framer vs Webflow](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/framer-vs-webflow) comparison covers what each one does better.


## Relume alternatives side by side


The last column tests Relume's signature step: can the tool turn a prompt into a sitemap, and on which plan? Pricing shows any free tier, then the cheapest paid plan and its billing basis.


Awesomic brings AI agents and vetted experts into one app. Start with a prompt to build a website, app, campaign, deck or video, then switch models or bring in a vetted expert without losing the project context. AI-agent plans start at $19/month, and expert plans start at $1,799/month.[See current plans](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


If the sitemap is the part of Relume you rely on, the five "Yes" rows are your shortlist; the rest replace a later step.


### 1. Awesomic


**Best for:** Skipping the export-and-rebuild step


**Overview:** Start with what's missing. Awesomic has no sitemap or wireframe generator, so we don't replace Relume's planning step; we replace the handoff after it.


Our agents build the site on a cloud computer reserved for the project, where the build keeps going with your computer switched off. Every plan includes one-click publishing to a live link and 200+ templates.


Page ten follows the rules page one set, because brand memory stores your brand, files and decisions.


A person can take over from the chat, too. Our All-in-One expert plan, bought separately, covers website and landing page design, UI/UX, Webflow and Framer builds, and copywriting, from a pool of 200+ vetted experts across 30+ skill sets. Hand-written React code needs a Dedicated expert, quoted on a call.


**Key features:**


- Several agents at once, each in its own chat, on the same project files.
- A lead agent that splits a big build across a team of agents.
- Connections to Figma, GitHub, HubSpot and Stripe, plus your own MCP servers.
- Projects you share with a link for client review.


**Pricing:** Each person's plan price is also their AI budget: $19 on Light, $99 on Basic, $199 on Pro and $499 on Studio, per person per month. These plans bill monthly, without refunds, and unused budget resets each month.


For current Awesomic plans and capabilities, see[the pricing page](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


The fee puts one person on Light at $219 a month before seat fees, by our math, and All-in-One's $3,219, which includes one Light subscription, at $3,419 or more, since the Terms don't say whether the bundled Light pays a second fee.


**Pros:** One-click publishing to a live link on every plan, no export or import between plan and site, brand memory across pages, Webflow and Framer builds by a vetted expert on a separate plan


**Cons:** AI-agent plans start at $19/month, and expert plans start at $1,799/month.[See current plans](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


**How to start using it:**


1. Pick Light, or start on All-in-One if you want a designer to build the site.
2. Read the checkout total, fee included, before paying.
3. Paste in your Relume page list, or describe the business.
4. Let the agents build, then ask for changes in the chat.
5. Publish to a live link and share it for review.


**Why it's a good Relume alternative:** You go from a page list to a live site in one place, with no Figma file or Webflow import in between.


**Final verdict:** Choose Awesomic when the export and rebuild are the slow part. If you'll miss the sitemap step, Octopus.do or Flowmapp is the better pick, and for a Webflow export alone, Relume Starter, at $18 per user on yearly billing, costs far less.


To put your first page live,[Get started](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) on Light.


### 2. Claritee


**Overview:** Claritee is built for the moment a client has to approve the plan. You start from a prompt or a URL, and it moves through three stages it calls Map, Layout and Design: a sitemap, then wireframes, then a designed layout.


Its pricing grid lists "Url to sitemap" and "Sitemap.xml to sitemap", so a redesign can start from the client's current site. Reviews run through share links, including comment-only ones on paid plans, and a Figma plugin imports your layouts from a Claritee public link.


**Key features:**


- A one-click interactive prototype built from your wireframes.
- Up to five hosted websites on a custom domain from the Teams plan.
- PDF and PNG export for clients who won't open a link.


**Pricing:** Free covers three projects of five pages each, with 10 AI actions a month. Pro+ is $50 per seat a year, or $5 per seat billed monthly, and Teams is $100 per seat a year, or $10 monthly, with viewers always free.


**Pros:** The cheapest paid plan for one person among the sitemap tools here, a sitemap from a client's existing site, free viewers for client review


**Cons:** No Webflow or React export published, hosting only from Teams, Pro+'s AI allowance reads "Unlimited" on its plan card but 500 a month in the comparison grid


**What agencies get from it:** A sitemap, wireframes and an approval link in one tool, so the client signs off before anyone designs.


**Final verdict:** Choose Claritee if you used Relume to get a plan approved and the Webflow export was never the point.


### 3. Flowmapp


**Overview:** Flowmapp maps a site in three layers: a visual sitemap, wireframe blocks for each page, and user flows that show how a visitor moves between them. It's aimed at studios that sell web design, and a cost estimator on every plan turns the page list into a proposal.


The AI sitemap generator starts on Pro, along with importing up to 1,000 pages from an existing site's URL. Exports go to Figma, PNG, XML, PDF and CSV, also from Pro. The Webflow, Framer and WordPress logos on its homepage sit under a "Win more clients" pitch; they aren't export targets.


**Key features:**


- User flows beside the sitemap, so journeys and pages get planned together.
- Cost estimation per project for client quotes.
- Unlimited pages and editors on Pro.


**Pricing:** Free gives you one project with 20 pages and no AI. Pro is $8.25 a month billed annually, or $15 monthly, Team runs $19.25 or $35, and paid plans come with a free trial.


**Pros:** AI sitemaps for $8.25 a month billed annually, user flows built in, Figma integration on Pro


**Cons:** No AI or export on Free, two sitemaps per project on every plan, no Webflow, Framer or code export


**Why studios pick it:** The plan, the flows and the estimate live in one file you can walk a client through.


**Final verdict:** Pick Flowmapp if you sell web projects and want the sitemap to feed the quote.


### 4. Mockflow


**Overview:** Mockflow now leads with its whiteboard, and its wireframing tool, WireframePro, is built in. Its AI sitemap page reads: "Enter a text prompt and AI creates a detailed, editable visual sitemap in seconds." The same AI drafts user journeys. That page doesn't tie either feature to a paid plan, only saying AI credits come on every plan, so Mockflow sits here by its cheapest paid plan.


The catch for Relume users is the handoff. Mockflow's pricing grid puts "Send designs to Figma, or turn them into code" on Max only, though another Mockflow page describes a free Figma plugin, so check your plan before counting on export.


**Key features:**


- AI sitemaps and user journeys on the same board as your wireframes.
- An MCP server for Claude or Cursor, and a Bridge that runs board AI on your Claude Code or Codex plan.
- An offline desktop app on Max.


**Pricing:** Basic is free for personal and nonprofit use only, with 100 AI credits a month. Plus is $9 per editor a month billed yearly with 800 credits, Max is $14 with 2,000 credits, and viewers are free.


**Pros:** Sitemaps, journeys and wireframes in one place, AI credits on every plan, low per-editor prices


**Cons:** Basic isn't for commercial work, Figma and code export are listed on Max only, the sitemap tool is one feature of a whiteboard


**Where it beats Relume:** One board holds the sitemap, journeys and wireframes, and a Plus seat costs half a Relume Starter seat, both billed yearly.


**Final verdict:** Choose Mockflow if your team already plans on a whiteboard and the wireframes can stay in-house.


### 5. Octopus.do


**Overview:** Octopus.do is the nearest thing here to Relume's sitemap step on its own. Its AI sitemap generator "creates visual website sitemaps from a short text description", each page gets content blocks and SEO fields, and the AI text draft works on every plan, Free included.


Its exports lean toward documents and WordPress. A Figma plugin exports a project "as high-fidelity wireframes, or visual sitemap", a WordPress export produces a WXR file, and DOCX and XLSX files cover the rest. Webflow's integrations page still lists an Octopus.do app, but Octopus.do withdrew it from the Webflow Marketplace on July 8, 2025.


**Key features:**


- ChatGPT and Claude apps, an MCP server and a REST API, added in August 2026.
- Branding and reusable symbols across pages on Pro.
- A Publish feature for simple, document-style websites.


**Pricing:** Free gives one user one project. Pro is $14 a month on an annual plan, or $16 month to month, for eight projects with Figma sync and PNG, PDF and CSV exports, and Team is $20 per user on yearly billing, or $24 monthly.


**Pros:** AI sitemaps on the free plan, Figma export as wireframes or a sitemap, a WordPress export


**Cons:** Free holds a single project and lacks PNG, PDF and CSV exports and Figma artboard sync, Publish makes document-style pages rather than designed marketing sites


**Why it's a good Relume alternative:** It keeps Relume's prompt-to-sitemap step without making you pay for wireframes and exports you won't use.


**Final verdict:** Pick Octopus.do if the sitemap was the only part of Relume you used every week.


### 6. Slickplan


**Overview:** Slickplan is a planning suite more than a sitemap generator. Its sitemap builder sits next to a content planner, diagrams and a site crawler that maps an existing site, and its AI page promises to "Generate sitemaps with a few words".


Where it differs from Relume is the destination. Slickplan's CMS plugins move a sitemap into WordPress, Joomla and Drupal, and you can share PDF, vector, image and DOCX files. Its Design Mockups tool is for uploading and reviewing wireframes you made elsewhere, not for generating them.


**Key features:**


- A site crawler that turns a live site into an editable sitemap, from Pro.
- A content planner for each page's content, beside the sitemap.
- CMS plugins for WordPress, Joomla and Drupal.


**Pricing:** A free version covers one sitemap for one user, and there's a 14-day trial with no card. Basic is $10.79 a month billed annually, or $11.99 monthly, but AI tools, the crawler and the content planner start on Pro at $31.49, or $34.99 monthly.


**Pros:** A CMS handoff Relume doesn't offer, a crawler for redesigns, three users on Pro


**Cons:** No Figma or Webflow export published, mockups are reviews of your own files


**What it adds that Relume lacks:** A route from sitemap into WordPress, Joomla or Drupal, which suits a rebuild on a CMS you already run.


**Final verdict:** Choose Slickplan for restructuring a large CMS site, and budget for Pro: AI sitemaps start there, which is also why it comes last in its group.


### 7. Figma


**Overview:** Figma is where Relume's Figma export lands, "Your whole project as a native Figma file, mobile variants and style guide included," in Relume's words. Dropping Relume means doing its early steps in Figma instead.


First Draft can "transform ideas into editable wireframes or designs", and since May 20, 2026, Figma's agent, still in beta and rolling out gradually, is its new entry point. Figma's help center notes the limit: it can't generate designs from your own design system. Past the design, Figma Sites publishes to a figma.site subdomain or your own domain, and Figma Make can push code to GitHub.


**Key features:**


- First Draft, reached through Figma's agent, for wireframes and designs from a prompt.
- Figma Sites (beta) for publishing from the canvas, on Full seats.
- Figma Make, with a push to GitHub.


**Pricing:** Starter is free with up to 500 AI credits a month. Professional runs $16 a month per Full seat, billed annually, with 3,000 AI credits a month, and Dev and Collab seats cost $12 and $3.


**Pros:** No import step for Relume's Figma files, publishing through Sites, code to GitHub through Make


**Cons:** No sitemap generator, First Draft can't use your own design system, Sites needs a Full seat


**Why a Relume user lands here:** The Figma files you exported from Relume open as they are.


**Final verdict:** Choose Figma if your team designs there anyway and the sitemap can live as a simple page list.


### 8. Framer


**Overview:** Framer is a website builder and host with an AI design agent, and Relume can't export to it.


Framer charges per site. Basic gives you a free first-year domain on yearly billing, 30 pages and two CMS collections, and Pro raises that to 150 pages and 10 collections with staging and branching. The trade is lock-in: Framer's help center says it "does not provide a way to export published sites as HTML files or static website bundles."


**Key features:**


- An AI design agent, with 1,000 credits a month on Basic.
- CMS collections for a blog or portfolio.
- Staging and branching on Pro.


**Pricing:** Basic costs $10 a site each month on yearly billing, or $15 monthly, and Pro costs $30 or $45. Each extra editor adds $20 a month on yearly billing, or $30 monthly, while viewers are free.


**Pros:** Design and hosting on one bill per site, a free first-year domain on yearly Basic, a free plan with 500 AI credits a month


**Cons:** No HTML export button, no sitemap step published, AI credits capped by plan


**What changes if you switch:** You design and publish in the same place, so there's no exported project to clean up.


**Final verdict:** Choose Framer if you were rebuilding Relume wireframes in Framer anyway.


### 9. Webflow


**Overview:** Webflow is one of Relume's three export targets, and Relume's export keeps "classes and structure intact" in Client-First naming. If tidying those classes was your complaint, building in Webflow from the start removes it.


Webflow drafts pages itself now. Its AI site builder generates up to five pages for a brand-new site on a paid Site or Workspace plan, or two without one. It only starts new sites, and what it drafts is a page structure rather than a sitemap. Paid Workspace plans can export HTML, CSS, JavaScript and assets, though CMS content, ecommerce and localized pages stay behind.


**Key features:**


- An AI site builder for new sites.
- Webflow CMS on the Premium site plan.
- Code export on paid Workspace plans.


**Pricing:** Site plans are per site: Basic runs $15 a month if billed yearly, or $25 monthly, and Premium, which adds the CMS, is $25 or $39. Workspace plans are a separate bill, starting with Freelancer at $16 a month billed yearly.


**Pros:** Hosting included in site plans, code export available


**Cons:** The AI builder only starts new sites, exported code leaves CMS content behind, site and Workspace plans are two bills


**Where it saves a step:** The page structure and the build share one tool, so there's no Relume import to tidy.


**Final verdict:** Choose Webflow if your Relume export was always headed there and you'd rather name your own classes.


### 10. Untitled UI


**Overview:** Untitled UI replaces Relume's last step, the component library, with one you buy once. The Figma kit lists "10,000+ components and variants" and "420+ page design examples", and the React library is built on Tailwind CSS and React Aria, with a free open-source tier.


There's a link to Relume worth knowing. Relume's paid Site Builder plans list "Untitled UI Webflow components", made with Untitled UI's creators, and Untitled UI also offers a free Webflow library on Webflow's Marketplace, last updated in November 2022. We found no shared ownership: they're separate companies working together.


**Key features:**


- A Figma kit with page examples to start from.
- React components on Tailwind CSS and React Aria.
- Lifetime updates on every paid license.


**Pricing:** Paid licenses are "Pay once, use forever in unlimited projects", with Figma Pro Solo at $129 and React Pro Solo at $349.


**Pros:** One payment instead of a monthly seat, matching Figma and React versions, a free React tier


**Cons:** No sitemap or wireframe AI and no hosting, its free Webflow library dates from November 2022, team licenses cost more than Solo


**What a one-time license buys:** A library you own outright, in Figma and in code.


**Final verdict:** Choose Untitled UI if Relume's library was the part you used and you mostly build in Figma or React.


## Which Relume step each one replaces


Price only matters once you know what each tool hands on. Here's the step each of the other nine takes over, its output and its cheapest paid plan.


Tool Relume step it replaces What it hands you Cheapest paid plan


Claritee Sitemap, wireframes Figma import, PDF, PNG, hosted pages on Teams Pro+, $50 per seat a year


Flowmapp Sitemap, wireframes, user flows Figma, PNG, XML, PDF, CSV Pro, $8.25 a month billed annually


Mockflow Sitemap, wireframes Figma and code on Max Plus, $9 per editor a month billed yearly


Octopus.do Sitemap, page content Figma plugin, WordPress WXR, DOCX, XLSX Pro, $14 a month billed yearly


Slickplan Sitemap, content plan CMS plugins, PDF, DOCX Basic, $10.79 a month billed annually; AI from Pro at $31.49


Figma Wireframe, design A published Sites page, code in GitHub Professional Full seat, $16 a month billed annually


Framer Build, host Framer hosting only Basic, $10 per site a month billed yearly


Webflow Build, host Webflow hosting; code export on paid Workspace plans Basic, $15 per site a month billed yearly


Untitled UI Component library A Figma file and React code Figma Pro Solo, $129 once


The "What it hands you" column decides more than the price. Relume handed you a Figma file, a Webflow project or React code, so pick the tool whose output lands where your next step happens. If it's the library step you're replacing, settle tokens and naming in a[design system](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/design-system) before you buy a kit.


## Get the sitemap right before the wireframes


Relume puts the sitemap first for a reason. In a 1998 Microsoft Research study,[Larson and Czerwinski](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/chi98_webdesign.pdf) gave 19 experienced web users three 512-item structures of encyclopedia content, with 128 items shared as search targets. Search tasks took 36 seconds on average in a 16x32 structure, two levels deep, and 58 seconds in an 8x8x8 one, three levels deep.


It's an old lab study on encyclopedia content, so read it as evidence that depth is a real decision, not a conversion figure. Plenty of sites still get structure wrong: the[Baymard Institute's navigation benchmark](https://baymard.com/research/homepage-and-category-usability) of 344 top-grossing US and European ecommerce sites found "76% of sites perform at a level of 'mediocre' or worse", with category taxonomy and main navigation among the weakest areas.


Some Relume users want its sitemap step followed by a different next step. In a 2024 r/webflow thread, one designer was[looking for Relume with design](https://www.reddit.com/r/webflow/comments/1fvur31/looking_for_relumeio_but_with_design_for_easy/) : "the flexibility of relume in terms of producing sitemaps" plus "fully (or somewhat) designed websites" for Webflow. It's one Reddit post, but it's the split this list follows.


So write the page list before you open any tool, and add a third level only when two won't hold the pages. To go from that list straight to AI-drawn screens, our[Uizard alternatives](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/uizard-alternatives) roundup covers prompt-first wireframing tools.


## What Relume really costs for one site


Publish and Export bill separately, and Webflow adds its own plan, so here is one site on each route, by our arithmetic.


Route for one site Per month, billed yearly Billed monthly


Relume Publish, Launch hosting only $12 $16


Relume Publish, Launch hosting plus Pro AI $26 $40


Relume Starter export plus Webflow Basic, five pages or fewer $33 $51


Relume Pro export plus Webflow Premium for the CMS $65 $97


Octopus.do Pro plus Framer Basic $24 $31


Awesomic Light plus the Platform Fee, one person Monthly only $219


Relume publishes no price for its higher AI usage tiers, so heavy AI use can cost more than the Pro AI row shows, and while Publish has no per-seat pricing, Export charges every user. Ours has a similar catch: Light's $19 is its whole AI budget, so heavier use means a bigger plan. The Webflow rows are two vendors' bills, and Webflow code export needs a paid Workspace plan on top.


If the real cost is a designer's time in Webflow, compare these totals with a[Webflow design subscription](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/webflow-design-subscription) , which swaps tool seats for someone doing the build.


## Relume competitors that didn't make the cut


A few Relume competitors came close. UX Pilot drafts screens and exports to Figma and code from its Pro plan, but it has no sitemap step. Balsamiq is low-fidelity wireframing with no free plan, and Webstudio is an open-source site builder rather than a planning tool.


## How to choose a Relume alternative


Pick among these Relume alternatives by the step that hurts, not the longest feature list. These pairings follow the groups above:


- If the sitemap is what you'll miss, try Octopus.do's free plan.
- If clients must approve the plan, use Claritee's comment-only links, from Pro+.
- If you're rebuilding a WordPress, Joomla or Drupal site, use Slickplan Pro.
- If your team lives in Figma, First Draft covers wireframes and a page list covers the sitemap.
- If you build in Framer, go to Framer directly.


Pairing a planning tool with a builder can undercut Relume's Pro export route, as the cost table shows. If you'd rather have a live site than a handoff, our agents build and publish it, and[our Relume comparison page](https://www.awesomic.com/alternatives/relume-alternative) covers when a pipeline like Relume's is the better buy.


## Where to start this week


Take one live project and run its page list through two tools from different groups, say Octopus.do for the sitemap and Framer or Webflow for the build. Time the trip to a reviewable page, and compare it with your last Relume project, cleanup included.


Keep Relume Free while you test; its one-page Figma export gives you a baseline to judge other[website design tools](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/website-design-tools) against.


## FAQ


### Does Relume host websites now?


Yes. Relume Publish went into beta on August 24, 2026, and its free tier keeps your site on Relume's own subdomain, badge showing, with traffic capped at 1,500 page views a month. Launch hosting, from $12 a site a month on yearly billing, adds your own domain and lets you drop the badge. A CMS followed on October 20, 2026, at no extra cost.


### Can Relume export to Framer?


No. Its export targets are Figma, Webflow, and React with Tailwind CSS and Shadcn UI, or plain HTML. Relume's Figma file can come into Framer through Framer's Figma plugin, and in the other direction, since Framer doesn't export published sites as HTML, Relume can start a new site from a Framer site's address. Neither move is a one-click export.


### Is there a free Relume alternative that makes sitemaps with AI?


Yes, two say so outright. Octopus.do's Free plan generates AI sitemaps for one project, within plan-based AI limits, and Claritee's Free plan gives you 10 AI actions a month for prompt-built sitemaps across up to three projects. Mockflow's Basic plan, for personal and nonprofit use, includes AI credits too. Flowmapp's free plan has no AI sitemap generator, and Slickplan's AI tools start on Pro.


### Is Untitled UI owned by Relume?


We found no sign of shared ownership. Relume's paid Site Builder plans include Untitled UI Webflow components, which Untitled UI's creators built inside Relume's library, while Untitled UI sells its own Figma kit and React library directly and gives away an older Webflow library on Webflow's Marketplace.


### Can Relume rebuild my existing website?


Relume's FAQ says you can "paste in your current website", and it builds a new site from it using its own components. If you want a site's look copied rather than rebuilt from Relume's library, our[Same.new alternatives](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/same-new-alternatives) roundup covers tools built for that.
